utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at some other cases that you discussed yesterday. If you remember, you looked at a large number of on-site investigations relating to various crimes. Now, one of which I'm interested in is the case of Dalip Dugoli. I don't intend to call up the exhibit on the screen, but your testimony in relation to this case was that this is a classical example of a terrorist attack on an Albanian civilian. He was attacked because he worked for the agricultural co-operative. Do you remember that case and your testimony in that regard?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, a number of the documents that we saw yesterday related to attacks due to the victims having been involved in Serb establishment jobs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at another one, and we will call up the exhibit in this case. It is D860. Now, while the exhibit is being called up, I will remind you that this is the case of Sejdi Muja, a forester from the village of Gradica, and he was shot on the 12th of January, 1998, when he left to go to work because he worked in Glogovac for the forestry estate there. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You also testified that he refused to boycott Serbian government institutions as ordered by the KLA. Now, how did you learn this, Witness, that this was the reason he was attacked?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection with this and other cases, where Albanian civilians were the victims of terrorist attacks because they worked in government institutions, I and everybody else engaged in this job came across this in the course of our work on individual cases or through operative information passed on to me by the prosecutor. And also in the course of investigations conducted against other persons who spoke about being subjected to pressure, forced to join the KLA terrorist gang, who spoke about being victims. This was one such case because before this he had reported more than once to the Glogovac SUP that he had been threatened followed, and he asked for protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: But that is information that would not be reflected in your on-site report?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This is not reflected because it is not something that has to enter the record of the on-site investigation, which has to contain only things immediately observed on site and does not include operative information gained before or after the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, from this document we see that the victim wasn't alone. He was with his neighbour, Selim Dibrani. That's in the second paragraph. And it reads: "On the morning of the day in question at about 0850 hours, the deceased and his neighbour Selim Dibrani set off to work in the direction of the village of Glogovac ..." Now, Selim Dibrani also worked in the Serb forest institute as did the victim, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you found this piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: It's in the second paragraph, first line.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it doesn't say here that he was also employed in the Serb forest institute, only that he was a neighbour of his and that they set out together.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Does it not say in the B/C/S translation "set off to work"?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't say where this person was employed. I only knew that the deceased worked for the forest company.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So you have no information on where Mr. Selim Dibrani worked?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. We'll move on to another topic. Ma'am, one of the first documents we looked at today was to do with the illegal MUP case. You've already mentioned it during this cross-examination. I don't think we need to go through the indictment and the judgement. I have some questions about this case. Now, as I understand it, a first-instance judgement was passed and this judgement was then confirmed on appeal, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I didn't say that because the judgement was changed, not confirmed. It's not the same thing. The second-instance court in Serbia found that some grounds of appeal by the defence counsel of the accused were well founded because they were appealing against the length of the sentence. So the trial judgement was changed in that the sentences were either reduced or increased, the sentences handed down in the trial judgement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Marinkovic, in the Milutinovic [sic] case when you were asked this question you said that: "After my investigation an indictment was issued, a first-instance judgement was passed. The Supreme Court of Serbia confirmed the judgement." Now, at the moment you're saying that that is not entirely correct and what you have said now is a more accurate representation of what happened?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, tell me what you're interested in particularly in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Please answer the question. I asked whether what you have said now is more accurate than what you had said in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said today is correct --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Milosevic case I don't know how it was entered in the transcript because I could not have said the sentence had been confirmed, as the second-instance judgement relating to these persons was in evidence. So it may -- I may have misspoken or it may have been misinterpreted, but I couldn't have said that it was confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And in that case, in the Milosevic case, you also said: "I stand by my cases and my work." Is that still your position, that you stand by your cases and your work?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at some documents in relation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I notice that page 49, line 5 we were dealing with the Milutinovic case, and we seem by line 16 to have moved to the Milosevic case. Were you meaning each of them?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I misspoke, Your Honours, in line 49 -- page 49, line 5. I should have said "Milosevic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was one thing, Your Honour, but secondly, may he we have a reference for what was put to the witness. May we see what the witness actually said. Was this a misinterpretation or what happened, as we do have the appeal judgement in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have the page, Ms. Gopalan?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours. It's page 223, and the 65 ter number is 3115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, going back to the illegal MUP case, have you heard of an organisation called the Human Rights Watch, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I hadn't heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: But now you are aware? You know of an organisation called Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let's have a look at a report that they have prepared, and that's 65 ter 6089. And while the document is being brought up, Witness, would you say that this case involving the Albanian policemen, this illegal MUP case, was professionally handled by all the parties involved?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "all the parties involved," who precisely are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll be more precise. By the prosecutors, the judges, that's whom I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both the court and the prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at the report on your screen. We have a past partial translation of the relevant section in the B/C/S, whereas the English version is a complete version. Now, if you can see in the cover page this is a Human Rights Watch report. It's entitled: "Serbia and Montenegro Persecution Persists: Human Rights Violations in Kosovo," and it's dated December 1996. You have that on your screen, don't you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And I'd like to now go to page 21 of the English and the next page of the B/C/S, please. And I'm going to read out a portion and get your comments. Now, it's a section headed: "The Case of the Former Albanian Policemen." And I'll read this out. "In November and December 1994, 134 [sic] ethnic Albanians were arrested for forming a parallel Albanian police force. All of them were formerly Yugoslav policemen and were active in the police trade union." Witness, this is the case that we have been talking about, correct, the illegal MUP case?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It says here 136 Albanians. I didn't investigate that number. Whether these are different ones or the same ones, I had 88 Albanians under investigation suspected of creating an illegal MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, apart from the number itself, which you say is not accurate, is the case the same case?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that this is a case here. This is simply a report by this organisation --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's right. This --

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I don't see what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: This organisation is reporting about the indictment and the judgement in relation to the illegal MUP case that we saw. Now, I'm going to take you in further detail in terms of what they say, but at the moment based on this information you would agree with me that this report relates to the same case, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the numbers do not correspond, names are not mentioned, so I cannot comment on something I know nothing about. I don't know on what basis this report was drawn up, no source of information is listed here, so that I as a practicing judge am not able to comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Very well, ma'am. Now, let me ask you the question another way. Were you aware of any other cases involving ethnic Albanians being arrested for forming a parallel Albanian police force in December 1994 and judgement being issued in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been in other district courts on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, but I'm not aware of what the number of such cases was.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So you don't know. Now let's move on, and perhaps we could deal with some of the questions raised. Let's go to the next page in the English, and I'm interested in the section, the paragraph that begins with "Fazli Balaj." Now, I'll read this out to you: "Fazli Balaj defended 12 of the former policemen, all of whom were arrested between November 24th and December 7th, 1994. He was allowed contact with some of his clients after six days. He told Human Rights Watch about one particular case of torture and the judge's response ..." Now, before we go any further, Fazli Balaj, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, but there is someone called Fazli Baljaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you know someone called Fazli B aljaj?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And it appears that he was a defence lawyer, and he defended 12 of these former policemen who were involved in the illegal MUP case, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a judge of the district court in Pristina. After 1992 he left the court of his own initiative, became a lawyer. He was a defence lawyer, but whether he defended 12 or one defendant, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So he was a defence lawyer, and the report states that he was involved in defending some of the policemen. Now, I'm going to continue reading. "He told Human Rights Watch about one particular case of torture and the judge's response. "'I went inside (the prison) to visit my client, Isak Aliu. He came to the corridor to meet me. When he came I saw that he was black and blue. I asked him to get undressed and I could he see that he had been beaten all over. 'At that moment, the jail door opened and the investigating judge, Danica Marinkovic, came in. I said to her, 'look what they did to my client.' She said, 'well, colleague, I am not a doctor. Address me in writing.'" Now, having read out the section, do you recall this encounter with Mr. Balaj in a prison?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam prosecutor, I have to disappoint you. This is not correct. I never went to the district prison. That was not my duty, nor is this incident described in the report correctly -- correctly described. It didn't take place.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you see or have this encounter with Mr. Balaj anywhere else if not in the district prison?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Fazli Balaj was the defence counsel for one of the accused I interviewed, he would have been present at the interview in my office. That is the only occasion on which we might have met. He would have been present at the interview. The public prosecutor and an Albanian/Serbian interpreter would also have been present. So if he had anything to state for the record, he would have been able to do so on that occasion. That was his right as defence counsel and it was never denied him.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And so your evidence then is that you don't recall ever having told Mr. Balaj to put his complaints about Isak Aliu in writing; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you're turning your question round, Madam Prosecutor. You asked me one thing a moment ago; now you're asking me something else. Please be precise in your questions so my answers can be precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Will you please answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you don't recall ever having told Mr. Balaj to put his complaints about Isak Aliu in writing?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you this was not correct. I did not meet him in the place or in the manner described here. We had no such encounter, so I couldn't have said anything to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, did you receive any complaints about the treatment of any prisoners who had been detained as a result of your investigations, had been detained in prison?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "complaints," what sort of complaints, about what?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mistreatment, beatings, for example.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There couldn't have been any complaints about such things because there never was any beating or mistreatment. I don't know who might have done such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I will ask this exhibit to be marked for identification, since I'm planning on returning to it shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my understanding, the witness did not testify to the contents of this document in any part of it, so I doubt that we can make use of it, even as marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While it's marked for identification, the Chamber won't make use of it, Mr. Djordjevic. But one of the purposes of marking it for identification is that foreshadowed by Ms. Gopalan, that is, she intends to return to the document for some other purpose, and the question of marking it, is simply to be sure we're dealing with the same document. So it will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1558, marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to call up 65 ter 3096, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll give you a moment to look at the document, Witness. Now, you can see that this is a document bearing the stamp of the Institute of Forensic Science in Pristina, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that this is the document of the Institute of Forensic Science in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And it is dated the 22nd of December, and it is addressed to you as the investigating judge, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that it's addressed to me, and I see that it says that upon the request of that court, Kio number 161/94 from the 22nd of December, 1994, a medical examination was carried out on the same day that my letter was sent, and the person was Isak Aliu.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Does this name, Isak Aliu, ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've just read it here now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: He was also the person mentioned in the Human Rights Watch report that we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, could we go to page 2 in English and page 1 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, before we go into the details, Witness, do you recall receiving this report?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall it now, but if it's addressed to me I must have received it. So it certainly must be in the case file because it's an official document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And let's have a look at the opinion section of the report. I believe it's at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S and it reads: "The injuries described under items 2, 3, and 4 of the report are haematomas, and under item 5 of the report there is an excoriation. They were all inflicted by a heavy blow from a blunt heavy mechanic implement, and individually and together they are qualified as a minor injury." Ma'am, you've said that you do not recall receiving this report specifically, but do you remember receiving these types of reports, i.e., reports of medical examination that had such conclusions, conclusions involving injuries inflicted during custody?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what, it does say here that this is a minor injury, but it doesn't say here who the injuries were inflicted by and where, so that your conclusion that these injuries were inflicted in custody is premature. I received such reports because in the course of an investigation anyone who was in detention and who applied to have a medical examination for any reason whatsoever was sent for a medical examination because that was their right, and I was regularly sent reports from the doctors involved, and depending on the severity of the health complaint further measures were taken for the treatment of these detainees. So I carried out my job in that respect. There may have been such reports, such as the one we see here. But as an investigating judge, when I get a report of this kind it's up to me to inform the prosecutor and the defence counsel. If they consider that there are elements of a crime here and that they know who the perpetrator is, they have the right to submit a criminal report against the perpetrator. The prosecutor and the defence counsel are the parties who can proceed based on this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So your testimony then is that it wasn't within your competence to further investigate that this was a matter for the prosecutor and defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prosecutor and defence counsel are authorised to proceed if they believe there are any steps necessary in that direction as part of criminal proceedings. It was up to me only to acquaint them with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is indeed. We will have the second break now, and we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Witness, when we left off we were looking at the medical examination report of Isak Aliu --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Which I'd like to tender into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could I call up -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, this will be Exhibit P1559, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could I call up D889, please. I'm not sure if this is the correct document. D889. I'm after the indictment dated 7th of April, 1995. Yes, that's right. And if we could go to item 27, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, this is the case of the illegal MUP that we were discussing during your testimony this morning. Do you remember? We looked at this document. And if we could go to item 27 in the English as well, we see that item 27 relates to an Isak Aliu. Now, ma'am, it is Isak Aliu's medical report that we've been looking at, correct, that we just saw before the break?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And I'll also point out some other indictees while we have this document up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If we could go to page 1, please. Page 1, item 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm just going to make a note of some of these names, since we're going to come back to them after this. In item 1 we have Avdija Mehmedovic, item 7 we have Bljerim Oloni, item 10 on the same page we have Murata Sahiti, item 13 --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sorry, the English page needs to be moved as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Item 13 we have Ramadan Ferizi.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And if we could now move to item 21 --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Who is Alidem Bejtulah. And the next page for items 38 Tahir Caka.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could we also see finally 32, please, for Bruti Sali [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, does this refresh your memory on the illegal MUP case?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let me just see if it's Bruti Sali. I'm not able to locate the last name at the moment, but I can provide that information later.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, I've listed a number of individuals who were indicted in this case, and I have with me medical reports, reports of medical examinations of these individuals that are similar to the ones that -- to the one that we saw for Isak Aliu. The conclusions stated in these reports are similar, if not identical, to what the report on Isak Aliu said. Now, let's call up one of these reports, 03105, just as an example. And just for the record Bruti Sali is item 39 in the indictment. That was the person who was missing. Ma'am, I'm not going to go through these reports individually, but as mentioned, I have eight other reports that bear the same conclusion, which is injuries sustained. Now, it would appear based on this document and the other medical reports that these indictees suffered certain injuries during their detention, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. They did suffer injuries, but we can't see when and what they were caused by. So as not to dwell on the findings too long, the answer is the same that I have given concerning the first one, Aliu or something. The same answer applies to all of them. Secondly, so as to inform the Trial Chamber, once I have interviewed an accused if detention is pronounced, they're held in the district court building in Pristina. They have no contact with anyone else. No one could injure them there. Also, concerning any visits in the prison, they can only be visited by counsel or by family members on a certain date and time. Rules are strictly observed. Concerning their situation and their complaints of certain types of treatment by those employed in the district prison, there is a judge tasked by the president of the court, who is under an obligation to visit the prison once a week, to visit each and every person detained and hear any complaints if there are any. All that is recorded and checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Very well, ma'am. Now, before I move on to the next document, I would like to tender into evidence the other medical reports relating to the indictees that I just referred to in the indictment. Would it be sufficient for me to read out the 65 ter numbers for these documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Neither Defence nor the Chamber have seen these documents before; therefore, I don't believe -- I believe that we should at least be shown these documents if they are being tendered now to verify whether they actually refer to the persons mentioned. I simply cannot take this blank statement that all of them were injured while in detention. We need to be acquainted with that, some basis should be lain for that, so that we may pose additional questions or objective we deem necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems to be required that you go through each, at least to identify the name. Would you proceed, Ms. Gopalan, or would you prefer to do that at a later stage of your examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I would prefer to do that at a later stage, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Particularly because these were exhibits that were referred to in the Milutinovic case as well. So in any event, I would have been asking for their admission right at the end. So I will move on and I will do it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean Milutinovic or Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Still keeping with this issue of Isak Aliu and the injuries that he suffered, could we go to a statement, and this is a statement of Fazli Balaj, so the defence counsel that we've just been discussing, and it's 06083. Now, ma'am, this is a statement that Mr. Balaj gave to this Tribunal, an investigator in this Tribunal, and it has been read back to him and he has stated that it's correct. And I also represent to you that he has initialled or signed each page. And I think it's only fair that you have the opportunity to comment on what he says about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If we could please go to paragraph 7 of the statement. If we could scroll up the page, please, I'll start with the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, this is Mr. Balaj's statement in relation to the detention of Isak Aliu. And he says: "During the first three days of their detention, my clients were not permitted" --

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologies. I don't see it in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The statement is not available in Serbian, Witness. I'm not showing -- I do not propose to show you the whole statement. I will read out the relevant portions and ask that you comment. And I'll start again. "During the first three days of their detention, my clients were not permitted any contact with an attorney. Neither the police nor Judge Danica Marinkovic would give me any information about their whereabouts." Now, what Mr. Balaj is saying here that information wasn't provided about the clients' whereabouts, is that true?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before answering I must say that I cannot comment selectively on the statement. I don't know what it is about in its entirety. As for the single part you read out, all I can say that it is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll read you out another part, and it's at the bottom -- yes. And that's paragraph 7. It reads: "Upon my request, Judge Danica Marinkovic eventually sent a request to the forensic medical department for an examination of Isak Aliu." I believe that is the document that we saw, the medical exam was a result of this request. Now I'll continue reading. "However, Judge Marinkovic waited until the 22nd of December, 1994, nearly a month of Isak Aliu's arrest to make this request. By this time, some of Isak Aliu's injuries had begun to heal. Today I have reviewed the medical certificate describing the results of Isak Aliu's examination dated the 22nd of December, 1994. It describes injuries to Isak Aliu's hands, back, hip, and right knee. The certificate would be sent to Judge Marinkovic for inclusion in her case file. After Isak Aliu received this examination and this certificate was produced, Judge Danica Marinkovic took no action to prevent further mistreatment of Isak Aliu or to prosecute those responsible for torturing him." That's the end of the paragraph. My question to you, Witness, is: Did you delay the request for the medical exam to nearly a month after Mr. Aliu's arrest, by which time his injuries had begun to heal?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. Everything in this paragraph is untrue, especially because there is no additional evidence or orders or Official Notes accompanied to this statement. Alongside his statement, Mr. Aliu should have forwarded the relevant documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: We'll deal with that in a moment. The last sentence: "After Isak Aliu received his examination and the certificate was produced, Judge Danica Marinkovic took no action to prevent further mistreatment of Isak Aliu or to prosecute those responsible for ... him." Now, you said that everything in this paragraph is untrue. This last sentence, that you "took no further action to prevent further mistreatment of Isak Aliu or to prosecute those responsible for torturing him," is that also untrue, that you -- so you took steps?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly, it is not true that there was any mistreatment or torture in the prison. That is not true. Secondly, concerning any medical findings for Isak Aliu, such as the one you have shown me at the beginning, I have provided an answer, and I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll ask this statement to be marked for identification, as I will be returning to it later as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1560, marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up 6076, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Marinkovic, we're moving on to 1995, the medical reports we saw for the end of 1994. Now, in your previous answer you mentioned relevant documents that Mr. Aliu should have forwarded. This would seem to be a relevant document. It is -- the date of delivery is the 27th of February, 1995, and it is addressed to you, Danica Marinkovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The complaint we see was sent to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And the English translation, the first paragraph, refers to certain accused. And we see that the name Isak Aliu is mentioned. Do you see that? So it's the same individual we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I he see him. He is the first one on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So this letter based on the dates would have been sent after you received the reports on the medical examination we just saw, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not convinced that the English document is the right document, judging by the contents and layout. It says here "submission of defence counsel." That would be the exact translation of the Serbian version, whereas in the English we have "complaint of the defending lawyer." First of all, we need to establish whether the establish translation reflects the original. The case number is the same, but it says "Cno" and in the Serbian it says "Kio." I'm definitely not convinced that this is the same document and on the face of it, it doesn't look like it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a Tribunal translation, Ms. Gopalan?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let me check that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, on whether it is a Tribunal translation, we are obtaining that information at the moment. But we can see from the document that this is a partial translation of the B/C/S. And as I understand it, it is the underlined portions in the B/C/S that have been translated to the English. And therefore, whatever I will be referring to in the English is available in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, if you find there is some material translation error in those parts of the document that are put to the witness, you may raise those as it occurs. Otherwise, please carry on, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Marinkovic, you said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honours, I must say that there seem to be significant differences between the copies. It says here "from paragraph 3 onwards ..." The B/C/S seems to be translated correctly, but the top part seems to be completely unrelated to the original. It is indeed not a complaint. It is a submission by defence counsel. That's number one. Number two, what I saw seems to be all right, but what follows is unclear. The only thing I was able to identify is the beginning of the third paragraph, which more or less could be considered a valid translation. However, all this I believe is insufficient to be of any use to the Chamber. "Complaint" and "submission" carry a different meaning. I have no problem against marking this for identification, but I would kindly seek that the entire document be translated, otherwise it shouldn't be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will determine that in due course. If you would carry on, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, you said that this was a document that you received based -- this was a complaint we see was sent to me, so you say it was sent to you, and the heading reads: "Complaint or submission of the defending lawyer." And the next line says: "This is the fifth complaint I have lodged in this instance." And I'm going to read to you the details: "On the 24th of February, 1995, I visited my defendants in the district jail. I informed them of the conversation I had with you in your office and about your refusal to examine the accused once again as you examined them once. "However, the accused Isak Aliu told me that on 17, 21, and 22nd February he was taken out of the premises of the jail and sent for interrogation to the state security premises in Pristina. On 22nd February 1995 he was subjected to physical torture." Before I continue reading, do you recall this visit you had from Mr. Balaj - I believe this is a document that he prepared, we can see that in the last page - in relation to conducting further medical examinations of his clients?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I he see here in the Serbian, it says "submission of the defence counsel," so it's not a complaint, it's a submission. And I will read, or rather, I have read the contents of this now --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, I --

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I cannot remember that Balaj --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, please continue.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he discussed this topic in my office. The only thing I can say is that in the third paragraph what he says here is in no way correct because Isak Aliu, after a decision had been issued on the conduct of investigations against him, could not have had a conversation with anyone nor could he have been taken away from the premises of the district detention unit in Pristina. So none of this can be true. There was no torture of the accused while the investigation was ongoing. This is not permissible nor is anyone authorised to do any such thing. So this is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So, ma'am, you don't remember Mr. Balaj having made such a request to you, to prevent torture, because there was no torture while the investigation was ongoing; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that there was no torture or mistreatment. This submission may have been made if there is the court stamp on it saying it had been received. I do know, however, that there was no torture or mistreatment that such things could not have happened. This submission I would have placed in the file, but there was nothing I could do, no action I could take, because he was not telling the truth. He is a defence lawyer so he has to write some things, he has to take some sort of action, so that's his right. I cannot prohibit him from writing whatever he likes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So your testimony then is that Mr. Balaj just made this up, these allegations?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say he made it up, but it's untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence and call up another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness doesn't recall this document, as I understand her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, but it is related to -- for other testimony that has been provided. And she did say that the complaint we see was sent to me. So it is a document that is addressed to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And there also appears to be the seal of the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I don't think she disputes the authenticity of the document either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that the Court mark this document for identification at the present and that the entire document be translated. It's true that the witness could not testify to the contents of the document at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything further, Ms. Gopalan?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, she did testify that "this submission I would have placed in the file," so not only does she say that it was a complaint that was sent to her, she accepts that it would have been the type of document that she was placed in the file -- that she would have placed in the file, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that. That's not correct. I apologise to the Chamber. I said that this was the usual sort of submission and that submissions of this kind were in case files, but I'm not saying that this particular document is one I received and placed in the case file. I don't remember that, but what is contained here about torture and mistreatment is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In view of the seal of the court, the Chamber will receive the document as an exhibit. If it appears to become material, the Chamber may order that the whole of the document be translated. At the moment that is not justified on what we have heard. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1561, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let's have a look at another document, Witness. This is 65 ter 06078. This is another document, also from Mr. Balaj. And we see in number 2 it says: "Examining magistrate of the Pristina district court." That would be you, correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see whether this document was received in the court. The content is similar to the content of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: We see in English it says "imprint of official seal."

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Is there another page in the B/C/S? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Right at the bottom, is that the official seal of the district court and the date of delivery?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the official seal of the court at the bottom of the document, but I don't know whether it was handed to me and the contents are not familiar to me now that I see the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Well, the contents are similar to the other document that we just saw. It is a continuing complaint about the treatment of Isak Aliu. And a number of recipients are listed in addition to yourself. And you say that although you are listed as a recipient, this is not a document that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with it. Nowhere do I see that it was handed to me personally or that I received it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, in this document we see somewhat more detail in relation to Isak Aliu's complaint, and could we go to page 1 of the English and page 1 of the B/C/S. This document names two individuals, state security officers, Rajko Dodera you see at the bottom of the B/C/S and perhaps -- yes, and same in the bottom of the English, state security officer Rajko Dodera, and it also names another state security officer from Ferizaj, that's on the next page, who says - it's in the English second paragraph - state security officer from Ferizaj, Zelenovic, has beaten him most. Now, ma'am, if you were to receive such information identifying members of the state security as having been involved in beating an individual in custody, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive this, a submission listing particular persons. This submission should have been sent to the district public prosecutor who was authorised to examine and establish whether what is stated in the submission is correct. I don't know either of the two people mentioned here, but Rajko Dodera is mentioned because a terrorist attack against him was launched, a hand-grenade was thrown on his house where he lived in Urosevac, and we mentioned this case yesterday. It's one of the exhibits in this case. So everything stated here was something that the district public prosecutor should have investigated, not I as the district judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, initially when we saw this document you said, I see the official seal of the court at the bottom of the document, but I don't know whether it was handed to me. And now having looked at it further you say that, "I didn't receive it." That's in line 17, page 72. What is it, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This submission was not handed to me as the investigating judge. It must have been handed to the president of the court, who forwarded it to the district prosecutor. It didn't arrive in my office, and I see the contents are similar to the contents of the previous document. So the defence counsel might have thought he had to address it to me as well. It does have the stamp of the court, but it was received in the clerk's office and then it would have been forwarded to the appropriate persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, during the course of this afternoon we've seen a number of documents relating to the treatment of Isak Aliu in custody that were addressed to you, and in relation to all of these documents your testimony is that you do not recall receiving them. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me whether what is mentioned here actually happened to Isak, then it's not correct because neither he nor any of the other accused who were in prison experienced anything like this. As for the submissions, I did not receive this last one, I don't recall the contents, so that none of this is familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to point out the translation into English. It has nothing to do with the original B/C/S. In the second paragraph of the English version it says on the 22nd of February he was beaten with truncheons on his back and arms, whereas it says here that on the 22nd he was taken to the state security station. And then again I see Pristina and a date, and usually CLSS says here that there is a stamp, but I don't see that on the translation. And then in the translation it says "complaint," whereas in the original it says "submission." So I really have a problem with these translations of these documents which I see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we have run over time and we cannot continue. We must therefore continue with this tomorrow when we sit. When we continue tomorrow, one possible way of dealing with Mr. Djordjevic's concern is to have the witness read the document, and it will then be translated in the course of the hearing. And that will be an instant translation which may not be as precise as a considered one, but it will have the advantage that we will be able to determine whether there is any material difference between what is said in the document in B/C/S and what is offered in the English translation. So we will adjourn on that basis and come back to the document tomorrow. I'm afraid we must adjourn now because the court is used for other purposes, and we are listed tomorrow afternoon at 2.15, when we will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
